newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar barely up in rangebound trade.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar barely up in rangebound trade.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices were trading slightly firmer at midsession, but the March contract remained unable to clear the 10.57 hurdle, floor sources said.
Speculative buying was met with producer selling at each tick higher, which kept the front month under pressure.
If the March contract manages to pierce 10.57 and climb to 10.60, the contract would attract short-covering by the speculators, who added to their short positions last week.
At 1140 EST, March was up 0.01 cent a lb to 10.54, having ranged from 10.57 to 10.49. Second-position May was trading 0.02 cent higher to 10.60, while the deferred contracts were 0.01 to 0.05 firmer.
Prices could creep gradually higher after falling to six-months lows last week, but March will need to pierce 10.63 to confirm the uptrend, dealers said.
Support was seen at 10.46, with major support seen at 10.29 and 10.21, basis the March contract.
Volume as of 1100 EST was estimated at only 4,187 lots.
Port authorities in Brazil said today sugar shipments from key ports reached 800,000 tonnes in October, compared with 730,990 tonnes for the same year-ago period.
